properties.name: Al-Haikk
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Sea of Claws

wiki.title: Alhaka
wiki.description: Alhaka, more commonly known as Al-Haikk (which means " City of Thieves " in Arabyan ), and also called El-Haikk, is one of the four great cities of Araby. Its surrounding lands forms an independent principality ruled over by the Padishah, also known as the Great Sultan of All Araby, the Emperor of all Araby. Arabyan corsairs demand tribute from foreign vessels that navigate the waters near Araby, although some of these ships are guaranteed safe passage by the Sultan of All Araby himself.

wiki.title: Martek
wiki.description: Martek is one of the four great cities of Araby. Its surrounding lands form an independent principality ruled over by a monarch with the title of caliph. The rulers and nobles of Martek are said to live in unimaginable luxury.

properties.name: Meknes
properties.source: The Voyage South (Novel) by Nicola Griffith

properties.name: Oasis of a Thousand and One Camels

wiki.title: Arjijil
wiki.description: The citadel of Arjijil is an infamous pirate's nest within Araby known as far as the Estalian Kingdoms. Said to be impregnable, the citadel looks over a precipitous cliff from which one can see the expanse of the Sahra, and at the base attempts at cultivating the region's poor soil. Arjijil is ruled by Alkadi Nasreen, Caliph of Mahabbah and who styles himself as the Lord of the Twin Seas (one such 'sea' being the Sahra).

wiki.title: Djambiya
wiki.description: Djambiya is an Arabyan port city, close to the Land of the Dead, to whose docks adventurers, explorers and fools of all kinds arrive, ready to enter the ancient ruins of the cursed land of Nehekhara. Djambiya is a very exotic city, full of music and aromas, where the natives, dressed in brightly coloured clothes, mix with the nomads of the desert, whose skin is full of ritual scars. It is not strange to see people from the Old World in this place, merchants and sailors from Estalia and Tilea, mercenaries, as well as some curious men in what appear to be knightly or priestly robes.

properties.name: Ras Karim
properties.source: Gotrek and Felix: Two Crowns of Ras Karim (Novel) by Nathan Long
notes: A port some hundred leagues east of Copher

wiki.title: Ras Karim
wiki.description: The port of Ras Karim is an Arabyan city located some hundred leagues east of Copher the City of Spices. Currently, the city is ruled by Caliph Halim il Saredi and his wife, princess Yuleh il Toorissi, who have obtained the throne thanks to a recent rebellion.

wiki.title: Fyrus
wiki.description: Fyrus is an island and porty city of the same name adjacent to the northern coast of Araby. It was once ruled by the Bretonnians of the Knights of Origo but has now returned to Arabyan rule after a great uprising against the foreign colonists.

wiki.title: El-Kalabad
wiki.description: El-Kalabad, also known simply as Kalabad, is an Arabyan trading port located in the Land of the Dervishes, on the western coast of the Gulf of Medes. In contrast to the inhabitants of El-Kalabad, the Kahied nomadic tribes to the north and the Ebonian tribes to the south shun settled civilization, preferring instead to live in the harsh desert as their ancestors did.

properties.name: Copher
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Sea of Claws

wiki.title: Copher
wiki.description: Copher, called the " City of Spice," is one of the four great cities of Araby. Its surrounding lands form an independent principality ruled over by a monarch known simply as the " Sultan of Copher ". Copher is located to the west of Al-Haikk, on the north coast of the Bay of Corsairs.

properties.name: Lashiek
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Sea of Claws

wiki.title: Lashiek
wiki.description: Lashiek, also spelled Lasheik, known as the " City of Corsairs," is one of the four great cities of Araby. Its surrounding lands forms an independent principality ruled over by a sultan who lives in unimaginable luxury.

wiki.title: Bel-Aliad
wiki.description: Bel-Aliad, know nowdays as the City of Dust, was a Nehekharan city later settled by Arabyans. It was destroyed by Arkhan the Black in -1149 IC. In its prime, it was called the City of Spices, but is also known as the City of Healers.

properties.name: Aiir
properties.source: The Voyage South (Novel) by Nicola Griffith

history.ruler_2512: Sultan Hamqa the Divine, Suzerain of Sadiz and Regal of all Kus

wiki.title: Aiir
wiki.description: Aiir is an Arabyan sultanate ruled by Sultan Hamqa the Divine Suzerain of Sadiz and Regal of all Kust. He is also an influent merchant who suffered greatly from the Magrittan Blockade in the last period. The captain of his mighty fleet which make port in Meknes is Mousaou Salah, while his daughter and his heir, Cendenai, is the captain of his flagship, the Rose of Aramam The first steward sometimes stays at court to manage the affairs of the Sultan.

properties.name: Amhabal
properties.source: Warhammer: Von Carstein Trilogy: Inheritance (Novel) by Steven Savile

properties.name: Zarekten
properties.source: Blood and Sand (Short Story) by Matt Ralphs

wiki.title: Zarekten
wiki.description: Zarekten was a city in Araby that guarded the entrance to the Great Erg to the south. It is one of the last frontiers between the settled Arabyan principalities and city-states of the prosperous north, and the nomadic Arabyan tribes who inhabit the desert to the south. Zarekten lies in a valley, protected by a moat carved by a river long since dried up.

wiki.title: Songhai
wiki.description: Situated in the south of Araby, the city of Songhai is ruled by a powerful King. Camel-trains making their slow way from north carry goods in the settlements throught the Sahra Desert. The King of Songhai has such eclectic tastes that he has more young eunuchs in his harem than wives.

notes: Located in the southwest of Araby, it is a vassal of the city of Aiir. Its ruler is Hamqa the Divine, Regal of Kust
